one_month_reasoning: Three scheduled or known events fall inside the window to 2026-11-08. (1) Q3 2026 results. Generac has not announced the date yet. StockAnalysis estimates Wednesday Oct 28 before the open, other calendars say Nov 4, and Q2 2026 was reported Jul 29, so the print is very likely inside the window. Expect the data-center backlog to step up now that the Amazon long-term supply addendum ($2.4B of 2027-28 deliveries, signed Sept 16) can enter orders; the Q2 call said none of the second hyperscaler was in the $1.6B backlog. That headline is largely known and priced: the stock rose 18.3% on Sep 17 and is +28% from the $175.11 Sep 16 close. Residential is the soft side: Q2 outages were more than 30% below baseline, and Kalshi puts only a 7% chance on more than 4 Atlantic hurricanes in 2026 (last trade $0.07, ~24.7k contracts). (2) Hurricane Isaias made landfall near Destin, FL after the Oct 9 close with 105 mph winds and Panhandle outages (WPTV). This is a small home-standby positive, and much of it was forecast before the Oct 6-9 rally. (3) The FOMC decides on Oct 28: Kalshi has a 25bp hike at 15% for October (~2.7M contracts) and 73% for December. Hikes are a mild headwind for housing-linked residential demand. These offset, so I hold no directional edge. I used a lognormal mixture centred at $225.5 (65% weight with sigma 12%, 35% with sigma 21% for the earnings jump), effective sigma about 15.7%. That is consistent with annual vol of 56% / 3.5 = 16% and with the 21-day log-return sd of about 14% in the openly visible Jul 31-Oct 9 daily history (StockAnalysis). The supervisor discounted my round-1 earnings-day statistics (keyed feed), so they no longer set the width; they agreed in direction with a fat-tailed event month.

bull.story: There is no separate 'second hyperscaler' award here: it is Amazon by inference (June 24 Global Purchase Agreement, finalised as the Sept 16 addendum), so that upside is already in the base case. The bull case needs new upside: Amazon purchases running toward the $8B warrant ceiling, first-hyperscaler orders extending into 2028, or a third customer, with capacity reaching ~$4B. FY27 beats to about $13.5 and FY28 reaches about $16.5 (+22%, near the S&P-implied $16.23 path). reasoning: Round 2 changes. (a) I removed every keyed-feed input (Alpha Vantage, Twelve Data). The FY27 EPS base is now the openly checkable $12.97 / $6.50B (StockAnalysis/S&P). The own-history leg is rebuilt from StockAnalysis's open quarterly ratio history (20 quarter-ends: forward P/E median 19.5x, IQR 16.7-22.6x, range 13.1-36.2x). (b) Multiples are now applied to horizon forward EPS ($14.07 = average of FY27 $12.97 and FY28E $15.17), which matches how StockAnalysis defines forward P/E, instead of 20.5x on FY27. (c) Shares are 60.0M, and GEV, BE and ENPH are out of the peer set with CARR in (core median 24.78x, verified). (d) Amazon is, by my inference, the second hyperscaler (no filing states it; the evidence is the matching June 24 date and global scope): The Q2 release says 'On June 24th, the Company secured a global supply agreement with a second hyperscale customer' and was negotiating '2027 and 2028 volumes'. The Amazon Transaction Agreement references a 'Global Purchase Agreement, dated as of June 24, 2026, by and between Generac Power Systems, Inc. and Amazon Data Services, Inc.'. The Sept 16 8-K gives $2.4B of 2027-2028 deliveries. The June 2 announcement was the first hyperscaler (~$700M for 2027). So I no longer count a separate second-hyperscaler award in the bull case, and I lowered the bull to $345 at 23%. The resulting fair value is $265: P/E $250.4 (50%), own-history $274.0 (30%), EV/EBITDA $287.4 (20%). I disagree with the supervisor's 15% DCF weight. At a 5.24% 10-yr yield and a 1.92 beta the DCF gives ~$124-144, which is 8.8-10.2x horizon forward EPS, below every quarter-end forward P/E GNRC has printed since 2021 (minimum 13.1x at the Sep 2022 trough). As a 12-month price anchor it lies outside the empirical range, so I use it to inform the bear tail, not the centre. Distribution: bear $150 / 25%, base $252 / 52%, bull $345 / 23%, each lognormal (sigma 0.34 / 0.26 / 0.28). The mixture has median ~$246, mean ~$258, log sd ~0.41, P(< -40%) ~10% and P(> +50%) ~19%. The median sits below the $265 fair value because of GNRC's reset history (Oct 2022 pre-announcement) and the +48% underlying growth consensus needs. Width: the openly sourced 16 rolling four-quarter windows (Q3'21-Q2'26 quarter-end closes) have a log sd of 0.52, the quarterly-return sd annualises to 52%, and Jul 31-Oct 9 daily realized vol is 59% (39% excluding the three largest days, which include the +18.3% Amazon day). That sample is dominated by the 2021-22 crash, so I set width a little below it, near the given 56% one-year realized vol, discounted for one-off deal days. The ladder is nearly unchanged from round 1 (P(>= $225) 0.59) because the corrections offset: the higher verified EPS and the removal of the keyed own-history leg (+), against the NTM basis, the extra shares and the removal of the double-counted second-hyperscaler upside (-). Limits: the openly visible daily price history covers only ~50 sessions. Comp pages are mandated, so in-lane sources are 9 of 26 overall and 9 of 16 (56%) excluding peer pages.
